questions.question: You’re at a party and your friend says, 'I really enjoyed your new book! It was so thought-provoking.' How would you best respond to show you appreciate their opinion?
options: Thanks! I’m glad you liked it. I worked hard on it.
Oh, it was just a quick draft—I didn’t expect you to read it.
I didn’t write it, so it’s not really my thing.
Actually, I didn’t finish it yet. It’s still a bit messy.
questions.answer: Thanks! I’m glad you liked it. I worked hard on it.

questions.question: Your colleague says, 'We should start the meeting early to avoid missing the first agenda item.' What would be the most appropriate way to suggest an alternative time?
options: Yes, that’s a good idea. Let’s do it at 9:30 instead.
I think we should keep it at 10:00; that’s usually better for everyone.
Maybe we should skip it and just focus on the next one.
I don’t know, it’s always better to be late than early.
questions.answer: I think we should keep it at 10:00; that’s usually better for everyone.

questions.question: You’re at a café and your friend asks, 'Do you mind if I borrow your phone for five minutes?' How would you respond politely but firmly?
options: Of course not! Go ahead and use it.
I’m sorry, I can’t give you my phone—I’m trying to finish my order.
I don’t have any phone to lend you anyway.
You can have it for ten minutes if you want.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, I can’t give you my phone—I’m trying to finish my order.

questions.question: Your friend says, 'I’ve been meaning to tell you—I really appreciate your help with the project!' What would be the most appropriate way to express gratitude and offer further support?
options: That’s okay, I’m glad I could help.
I didn’t do anything special, so don’t mention it.
I’m glad you think so! Let me know if you need anything else.
Actually, I’d prefer not to discuss it further.
questions.answer: I’m glad you think so! Let me know if you need anything else.

questions.question: In a formal email to a professor, you want to express that you disagree with their suggestion but still show respect. What would be the most appropriate opening line?
options: I completely agree with your idea and would love to discuss it further.
I’m sorry to disagree, but I think we should consider another approach.
Your suggestion is interesting, but I’d like to propose an alternative method.
I don’t think this will work—maybe you should try something else.
questions.answer: Your suggestion is interesting, but I’d like to propose an alternative method.
